reject.reason: The camp's own note calls it "the eastern option for MOUNT HINMAN". Hinman is joined to Daniel by a ~6,200 ft col, and the Daniel-to-Hinman traverse from Peggy's Pond is documented (SummitPost forum thread on the Daniel-Hinman traverse; Wenatchee Outdoors Daniel & Hinman page). Removing it on the grounds that Daniel's massif lies between them ignores that parties cross it.

reject.camp: Necklace Valley — Jade, Emerald and Opal Lakes
reject.reason: [medium] The reviewer KEPT La Bohn Gap for this route because it sits on the Daniel-Hinman crest. From the west, the only way to La Bohn Gap is up Necklace Valley, and the Lynch Glacier drops toward Pea Soup Lake on the Foss side. Keeping the Gap while cutting the valley below it is inconsistent: either both stay or both go. I lean keep.

reject.reason: The Headlight note says it is the staging camp for parties "approaching the north side via Stuart Pass". The Goat Pass note (kept for this route) says Goat Pass is the high camp for the Stuart Glacier Couloir "when approaching from the Ingalls side". SummitPost also gives a south approach to the couloir via Goat Pass across the upper Stuart Glacier. The route's own approach ends under the col shared with the West Ridge, which is the Goat Pass side.

reject.camp: Upper Ingalls Creek meadows, below Stuart Pass
reject.reason: Same Ingalls-side approach. The meadows at the head of Ingalls Creek are on the walk from Ingalls Lake/Stuart Pass to Goat Pass, which the reviewer keeps for this route.

reject.camp: Ingalls Creek basin camp, below Longs Pass
reject.reason: The Goat Pass camp note (group 23) calls Goat Pass "the camp for the southern approach over Longs Pass and up Ingalls Creek" and says "the Cascadian Couloir descent drops back the same way". A north-side party on the Ingalls approach both goes in past this camp and descends to it.

reject.camp: Ingalls Creek basin camp, below Longs Pass
reject.reason: The Gendarme is reached only by climbing the North Ridge, and the reviewer keeps Headlight and Goat Pass for it, so the Ingalls-side approach is accepted. That approach runs over Longs Pass and up Ingalls Creek, and the standard descent is the Cascadian Couloir, which ends back in Ingalls Creek at this camp (Goat Pass note). This is exactly the case of north-side parties using the Cascadian descent.
